title: Upgrading to 0.22: LLM Framework Transition

book.title: NVIDIA NeMo Guardrails Library Developer Guide

description: How NeMo Guardrails 0.22 routes engines through the new DefaultFramework, when LangChain is still required, and how to opt in.
content:
Upgrading to 0.22: LLM Framework Transition NeMo Guardrails 0.22 introduces a DefaultFramework that talks to OpenAI-compatible endpoints directly over httpx , with no LangChain dependency on the request path. As a result, langchain and the provider-specific langchain-* packages are now development-only dependencies of nemoguardrails . The guiding principle is: Prefer DefaultFramework whenever the underlying wire protocol is OpenAI-compatible. Use LangChain only as the fallback for engines whose API is not OpenAI-compatible. This guide explains how the routing works, when you need to install LangChain, how to migrate legacy engine: vllm_openai configs, and how to control the active framework. Your existing config keeps working If your config.yml uses one of the four engines below, the upgrade is silent: the same pip install nemoguardrails install pulls everything you need, and your config does not change. Engine Default base URL openai https://api.openai.com/v1 nim https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1 nvidia_ai_endpoints https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1 (alias for nim ) ollama http://localhost:11434/v1 These engines are routed to DefaultFramework , which builds an OpenAIChatModel against an OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoint. You can override the endpoint by setting parameters.base_url and the API key by setting parameters.api_key (or the engine-specific environment variable, for example OPENAI_API_KEY , NVIDIA_API_KEY ). models
type: main
engine: nim
model: meta/llama-3.1-70b-instruct
parameters
temperature: 0.0
max_tokens: 1024
No code change, no new install command. OpenAI-compatible self-hosted and third-party endpoints Many providers expose an OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions route. For all of them, the recommended migration is: Use engine: openai plus parameters.base_url . Do not use engine: vllm_openai and do not set NEMOGUARDRAILS_LLM_FRAMEWORK=langchain . Examples that fall under this pattern: vLLM with the OpenAI-compatible API ( python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server ). TGI / Hugging Face TEI when deployed with /v1/chat/completions enabled. OpenRouter at https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 . Together.ai , Fireworks.ai , Groq . DeepSeek at https://api.deepseek.com/v1 . llama.cpp server with --api . Any other “OpenAI-compatible” self-hosted endpoint. Migrating a legacy vllm_openai config If your old config looked like this: models
type: main
engine: vllm_openai
model: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
parameters
openai_api_base: http://localhost:5000/v1
Migrate to: models
type: main
engine: openai
model: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
parameters
base_url: http://localhost:5000/v1
api_key: EMPTY
When self-hosted vLLM does not enforce authentication, set parameters.api_key to any non-empty placeholder such as EMPTY . If your deployment requires a real token, replace it with that value or load it through api_key_env_var . The legacy engine: vllm_openai form is still recognized by the LangChain framework, but for new configurations the DefaultFramework form above is preferred. When you need LangChain Engines whose API is not OpenAI-compatible still require LangChain. To use them you must: Install LangChain plus the provider-specific package yourself. Set NEMOGUARDRAILS_LLM_FRAMEWORK=langchain for the process. Engine names in config.yml stay bare ( engine: anthropic , engine: cohere , …) — there is no langchain/<provider> prefix syntax. Examples that genuinely need LangChain: vertexai (Google Vertex AI). google_genai (Google Generative AI via LangChain). anthropic (Anthropic Claude). cohere . azure (Azure OpenAI uses a deployment-name URL plus api-version query string that the DefaultFramework’s OpenAI-compatible client does not currently support). huggingface_pipeline / hf_pipeline_* (in-process Python pipeline). huggingface_hub . huggingface_endpoint (default text-generation schema; if your endpoint exposes /v1/chat/completions , prefer the DefaultFramework engine: openai plus parameters.base_url instead). trt_llm (TensorRT-LLM in-process). self_hosted (LangChain self-hosted wrapper). Install command pip install langchain langchain-<provider
For example, to use Anthropic Claude: pip install langchain langchain-anthropic
For Cohere: pip install langchain langchain-cohere
For Azure OpenAI: pip install langchain langchain-openai
The provider package list is the same as the LangChain integration list. See the LangChain chat-model integrations page for the full set of community providers. Activating the LangChain framework Once LangChain and the provider package are installed, set the environment variable so the framework registry routes through LangChainFramework , and use the bare engine name in config.yml : export NEMOGUARDRAILS_LLM_FRAMEWORK=langchain
models
type: main
engine: anthropic
model: claude-3-5-sonnet-latest
parameters
temperature: 0.0
The framework name is global to the process. If you previously used engine: anthropic or engine: cohere directly without setting the variable, that path now fails — DefaultFramework does not know about those engines. Set NEMOGUARDRAILS_LLM_FRAMEWORK=langchain before the process starts. The legacy provider-named engines ( anthropic , cohere , vertexai , azure_openai , deepseek , huggingface_endpoint , huggingface_pipeline , huggingface_hub , trt_llm , self_hosted , vllm_openai , …) all keep working under the LangChain framework. No engine renames are needed; install the matching langchain-<provider> package and toggle the env var. To see the full list of engine names the LangChain framework recognizes, run: NEMOGUARDRAILS_LLM_FRAMEWORK=langchain nemoguardrails find-providers
Choosing the active framework NeMo Guardrails resolves the framework name in two places: The NEMOGUARDRAILS_LLM_FRAMEWORK environment variable, read once when the framework registry initializes. The default value is default . The set_default_framework(name) function, which mutates the registry at runtime. Environment variable Set NEMOGUARDRAILS_LLM_FRAMEWORK before starting the process: export NEMOGUARDRAILS_LLM_FRAMEWORK=langchain
nemoguardrails chat --config=path/to/config
Accepted values: default (default) - the new httpx-based path. Engines openai , nim , nvidia_ai_endpoints , ollama , plus any other OpenAI-compatible provider configured with engine: openai and parameters.base_url . langchain - all engine resolutions go through LangChainFramework . Useful when every model in your config is a LangChain provider. Any name you have registered yourself with register_framework(name, instance) . Programmatic switch from nemoguardrails import set_default_framework
set_default_framework("langchain
set_default_framework raises KeyError if the name has not been registered and is not one of the lazy-loaded built-ins ( default , langchain ). Registering a custom framework from nemoguardrails import register_framework, set_default_framework
from my_pkg import MyFramework
register_framework("my-framework", MyFramework
set_default_framework("my-framework
register_framework raises ValueError if a framework with the same name is already registered. Common errors “No default base_url for provider ‘X’” ValueError: No default base_url for provider 'cohere
Set it explicitly in model parameters: parameters.base_url
This error comes from _resolve_base_url in nemoguardrails/llm/frameworks/default.py . It means the engine name you used (here cohere ) is not in DefaultFramework ’s routing table and is not an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Fix: either supply a parameters.base_url for an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or set NEMOGUARDRAILS_LLM_FRAMEWORK=langchain and install langchain-cohere (the engine name in config.yml stays cohere ). “Framework ‘X’ is already registered” register_framework does not allow rebinding. Either pick a different name or, in tests, call the registry-reset hook before re-registering. “Unknown framework ‘X’” set_default_framework was called with a name that is not registered and is not one of the lazy built-ins default or langchain . Register the framework first, or correct the name. Unsupported parameter '<name>' (or Unrecognized request argument ) on first call 0.22 forwards parameters from config.yml directly to the OpenAI-compatible HTTP client when an engine routes through DefaultFramework . Keys that LangChain accepted as Python flags ( streaming , disable_streaming , verbose , cache , callbacks , tags , metadata , name , model_kwargs ) and provider-prefixed credential aliases ( openai_api_base , nim_base_url , *_api_key , …) are not part of the OpenAI wire shape and are rejected by the provider. NeMo Guardrails detects the recognizable shapes at boot and on the first 400/422 response, and appends a hedged migration hint to the underlying provider error. Fix paths: Adapt the config to OpenAI-compatible shape. Rename openai_api_base → base_url , drop LangChain Python flags, remove provider-prefixed aliases. The migration recipe in OpenAI-compatible self-hosted and third-party endpoints covers the common case. Keep the 0.21 config. Set NEMOGUARDRAILS_LLM_FRAMEWORK=langchain for the process and install LangChain plus the matching provider package. The legacy field names continue to work under the LangChain framework. What does not change in 0.22 Streaming. stream_handler , stream_async , and the rails-level streaming flag work the same as 0.21. No config changes required. Tool calling. tools , tool_choice , and provider-side function/tool calling continue to work. The LLMResponse.tool_calls shape is unchanged. Reasoning configs. reasoning_config: {remove_reasoning_traces: ..., start_token: ..., end_token: ...} is unchanged. Reasoning models (DeepSeek R1, NIM nemotron-reasoning , OpenAI o-series) keep working under both frameworks. Custom providers registered in config.py . Calls to register_chat_provider(name, cls) and register_provider(name, cls) continue to work. They register on the active framework — DefaultFramework if no env var is set, LangChainFramework if NEMOGUARDRAILS_LLM_FRAMEWORK=langchain is set. Providers registered for one framework are not visible to the other; if your config.py needs to support both modes, register on each: from nemoguardrails.llm.frameworks import get_framework
get_framework("default").register_provider("my_engine", MyLLMModelClass
get_framework("langchain").register_provider("my_engine", MyLangChainProviderClass
Caching, telemetry, callbacks, embeddings. No 0.22 changes affecting these. Provider matrix and supported LLMs For the full engine-to-framework matrix, including streaming and tool-calling support per engine, see the Routing matrix in Supported LLMs . Related references Configuration YAML Schema Reference - all models.* fields, including parameters semantics for both frameworks. LangChain Integration - using RunnableRails , agent middleware, and chains as actions. Custom LLM Providers - registering a provider inside a framework
summary: NeMo Guardrails 0.22 introduces a DefaultFramework that talks to OpenAI-compatible endpoints directly over httpx, with no LangChain dependency on the request path. As a result, langchain and the provider-specific langchain-* packages are now development-only dependencies of nemoguardrails.
